newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SANDERS ALLOWS ONE UNEARNED RUN AS PADRES EDGE PHILS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SANDERS ALLOWS ONE UNEARNED RUN AS PADRES EDGE PHILS.

text.p: Scott Sanders allowed one unearned run and four hits over eight innings as the National League Western Division-leading San Diego Padres edged the Philadelphia Phillies 2-1 Wednesday.
Sanders (9-4) walked two and struck out three before Trevor Hoffman pitched a 1-2-3 ninth for his 34th save.
Sanders is 5-0 with a 1.67 ERA in his last six starts and has won eight of his last nine decisions.

"When I was warming up I knew I was going to have trouble keeping the ball down tonight," Sanders said. "But every time I was close to getting into a jam I was able to throw a strike and get them to hit it to someone."
The Padres scored single runs in the first and third innings off Philadelphia starter Matt Beech (1-3).
Tony Gwynn had four hits and scored both San Diego runs.
"I didn't play yesterday because I fouled a ball off my big toe and it swelled up like a balloon," said Gwynn, who had the 28th four-hit game of his career. "I felt a lot better today."

In New York, Carl Everett's chopper to second with one out in the bottom of the 12th allowed Alvaro Espinoza to score the winning run as the Mets edged the Los Angeles Dodgers 3-2, salvaging the final game of a three-game series.
The loss dropped the Dodgers one game behind the Padres for the lead in the National League West. Los Angeles finished its nine-game East Coast swing at 6-3.
The Mets won for just the third time in their last last 13 games and are now 3-6 under manager Bobby Valentine.

In St Louis, John Mabry belted a two-run homer and Tom Pagnozzi added a pair of solo shots as the Cardinals defeated the Houston Astros 6-4, sweeping the three-game series that put them back on top in the N.L. Central.
The Cardinals have a 1 1/2 game-lead over the Astros, who have lost four straight.

Andy Benes (16-9) tossed seven-plus innings and allowed two runs and four hits, walked two and struck out five to become the National League's third 16-game winner. Dennis Eckersley allowed a run and two hits over the final 1 1/3 innings to post his 26th save.
Donne Wall (9-5) took the loss, pitching six innings and giving up five run.
Brian Hunter homered for Houston.

In Cincinnati, Willie Greene had a two-run triple and a three-run homer for a career-high five RBI as the Reds roughed up Tom Glavine to complete a three-game sweep of the major league-best Atlanta Braves 12-6.

Bret Boone had three hits and three RBI and Kevin Mitchell went 3-for-3 with a two-run homer for the Reds, who swept the Braves for the first time since 1992. Cincinnati has won four of five. Atlanta (84-55) lost its season-high fifth straight.
Roger Salkeld (7-4) in five innings of relief gave up one run and three hits over five innings for the win.
The Reds pounded Glavine (13-9) for eight runs and nine hits over four innings as the Braves were swept for the first time this season. The eight earned runs are the most ever given up by Glavine.
At Florida, Kevin Brown won his fifth straight and Jeff Conine had a three-run double and four RBI to power the Marlins to a 9-2 rout of the Chicago Cubs in the rubber game of a three-game series.
Brown (15-10) allowed two runs -- one earned -- and five hits with one walk and three strikeouts before tiring in the ninth. Yorkis Perez struck out the final two batters.

During his five-game streak, Brown has allowed just seven runs -- six earned -- and 27 hits with 35 strikeouts over 40 1/3 innings. He lowered his major league-leading ERA to 1.88, recorded his franchise-record 15th victory of the season and got his 1,000th strikeout.
Florida has won 10 of its last 12 games.

In Montreal, rookie right-hander Jose Paniagua and Mel Rojas combined on a three-hitter and Moises Alou homered and drove in three as the Expos shut out the San Francisco Giants 6-0 for their fifth consecutive victory.
Paniagua (2-2), in his seventh major-league start, took a no-hitter into the eighth before allowing a double to Rick Wilkins. He walked three and fanned six.
Mark Grudzielanek also homered for Montreal.

In Pittsburgh, Jon Lieber came within one out of his second career complete game and Mark Johnson hit a two-run homer as the Pirates defeated the Colorado Rockies 5-2 for just their second win in seven games.
Lieber (7-5) allowed two runs and nine hits with five strikeouts. Dan Plesac got the last out.
Al Martin also homered for Pittsburgh.
